summary: Round 15 verifies three things and finds one new matrix gap. (1) All three round-14 minors landed: the truncated duplicate of the saturation sentence is gone -- 'saturation clause matters' now occurs exactly ONCE, at SPEC.md:462, and no line ends on 'alone is' except that sentence's own wrap; criteria parse 1..12 in both the scope list (109-158) and the acceptance list (386-475) with no duplicate and no gap. (2) The T1 GET row at :497 carries 'every replay answered WITH ITS OWN original offsets' and names my mutation in its column ('answering all six from the pointed delta's first run'). (3) The ambiguous-commit row landed verbatim at :496. BUILDABILITY VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY, not assumed: in a review tree I drove a real LocalSequencer with a CheckpointWriter (checkpointEveryDeltas=1) whose log store was swapped to FaultInjectingStore(Faults(0, 1.0, 0)) after start; commitAll threw 'injected: the write landed but the response was lost' AND the delta was present in the backing store afterwards (p/ctl/log/0/.../0000000000000001.delta) with NO ckpt/ object -- i.e. exactly 'the PUT landed, commitAll threw, observe never ran', constructible today with no M4.12 dependency. One caveat for the M4.10d session, recorded as a finding below only in note form here: Faults(0,1.0,0) applied from process start ALSO faults CommitLog.open inside LocalSequencer.start (measured: IOException at FaultInjectingStore.java:247 via CommitLog.java:382), so the row needs a test-local switchable delegate or a seeded p<1 run -- the existing fault store alone is necessary but not sufficient. The one new finding is a below-watermark replay case that criterion 6 requires and no row constrains.

findings.title: Criterion 6's below-watermark clause claims the T0 row rejects a refuse-below-the-watermark dedup; the T0 row as worded does not, and every row in the matrix is at-the-watermark
findings.failure_scenario: Criterion 6 now says 'Below that watermark, a replay the pointed delta DOES carry is answered too; refusal is permitted ONLY when the pointed delta does not carry the triple', and then asserts 'a dedup that ... refuses below the watermark without reading, satisfies neither this criterion nor the T0 row'. The second half of that sentence is false against the T0 row as written. The T0 row at :493 says 'Idempotent commit on (podId, incarnationId, flushSeq) replay, including post-checkpoint', and its mutation column names only two mutations: fresh-offset assignment and bare-pair keying. A post-checkpoint replay is a replay of flushSeq N where lastAppliedFlushSeq == N -- AT the watermark, not below it -- so nothing in the row requires a fixture with flushSeq strictly less than the watermark, and refusal is not fresh-offset assignment. The other two idempotency rows are at-the-watermark too: the ambiguous row (:496) reconciles a commit the window never recorded, so no watermark is above it, and the GET row (:497) has six pods each replaying its own most recent flushSeq -- its 'always-refuse dedup' clause kills a dedup that refuses EVERYTHING, not one that refuses only below. The reachable production consequence: one commitAll carries flushSeq 4 and 5 from pod A (ADR-0036 itself says 'A batch may carry several requests from one pod -- commitAll is the primitive -- and <= handles a replay of the lower of them', and BatchingSequencer.java drains a shared queue, so nothing separates two flushes of one pod into two batches). Both land in ONE delta; the pointer names it; the watermark is 5. A retry of 4 -- the case where the producer's ack for 4 was lost -- is below the watermark and IS carried by the pointed delta, so criterion 6 requires it be ANSWERED. A dedup that short-circuits it to a refusal ships green on the whole matrix while handing a producer a hard error in exactly the lost-ack case M4.10 exists to make safe. Remedy is one clause, not a new row: extend the T0 row to '... including post-checkpoint AND a replay BELOW the watermark that the pointed delta carries (two flushes of one pod in one commitAll)', and add to its mutation column 'a dedup that refuses everything strictly below the watermark without reading the pointed delta'. Non-blocking: this is the M4.10d test author's obligation and the round budget is spent -- record it as a minor in the commit body per review.md `minors-land` rather than opening round 16.
findings.surviving_mutation: In the dedup path, guard the pointed-delta lookup with `if (flushSeq < lastAppliedFlushSeq) throw new IOException("replay below the watermark");` and keep the exact-match lookup only for `flushSeq == lastAppliedFlushSeq`. Green on the T0 row (its replay is at the watermark, and refusal assigns no fresh offsets), green on the ambiguous row (no watermark above the unobserved commit), green on the GET row (six pods each at their own watermark, one GET, each answered with its own offsets) -- and it violates criterion 6 for every replay of the lower flushSeq in a multi-flush batch.
